title: A counterexample to the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture
main_claim: The paper claims there are arbitrarily large graphs G with alpha(G)<=2 and mu(G)+1 < |V(G)|/2 <= chi(G), which would disprove chi <= mu+1. A stronger form is also claimed: every well-signed matrix with one negative eigenvalue has rank > |V|/2+1, so kappa(G)+1 < |V|/2 <= chi_f(G). The graphs are clique blow-ups H[s] of finite-field "hole"-relation base graphs H that satisfy three conflict properties (G1)-(G3).
sibling_notes: The board for family 157 (hive:oai_math:review:fam:157) was empty when I checked, so no sibling input was used. The paper cites companion OpenAI preprints (the Hadwiger counterexample and the linear list-Hadwiger bound) only for a remark and for Corollary 1.4. The main proof does not depend on them, so there is no circular dependence.
